title: Push-Pull Test Track
intro: Same car, same floor. Change one thing, predict what happens, release, and read the data.
note: This is a model that uses the lesson's backup numbers. The real gentle-and-strong push test and the stopper build with a toy car still count. The lesson gives no numbers for push versus pull, so that round only shows the direction. Read aloud: a push moves it away from you, a pull moves it toward you.
summary: A push or pull can start, stop, or turn motion. A strong push sent the car 6 tiles, a soft push 2 tiles. A pull brought the car toward you. Foam stopped the car 3 of 3 tries and cardboard 1 of 3, so the evidence picks foam.

rounds.question: Same car, same floor, same starting line. How far does a push send the car?

predict.q: How many tiles will it go?

options.label: Soft push
options.hint: a soft push gives the car a little motion, not a lot.

options.label: Strong push
options.hint: a strong push gives more motion than a soft push did.

reads.q: What did changing the push strength do?

choices.label: The strong push sent the car farther.
choices.why: Yes. Soft went 2 tiles, strong went 6 tiles.

choices.label: Both pushes went the same distance.
choices.why: Look at the marks: 2 tiles and 6 tiles are not the same.

choices.label: The soft push went farther.
choices.why: Soft went 2 tiles and strong went 6 tiles. 6 is more than 2.

rounds.finding: Soft push: 2 tiles. Strong push: 6 tiles. A stronger push changed the motion more.

rounds.question: Now change the direction. Which way does the car go?
held: Same strength of push or pull

predict.q: Which way will the car go?

options.label: Push it
options.hint: a push moves something away from you.

options.label: Pull it
options.hint: a pull moves something toward you.

choices.label: Moving a wagon toward you
choices.why: Yes. A pull moves something toward you.

choices.label: Kicking a ball away from you
choices.why: Kicking sends the ball away. That is a push.

choices.label: Letting the car sit still
choices.why: No push or pull means no change in motion.

rounds.finding: A push moved the car away from you. A pull moved it toward you. Same strength, opposite directions.

rounds.question: The car rolls too far past the line. Which stopper stops it?

predict.q: Out of 3 tries, how many times will it stop the car?

options.label: Foam stopper
options.hint: foam is soft and squeezes; it can grab the car.

options.label: Cardboard stopper
options.hint: thin cardboard can bend and let the car roll past.

reads.q: Which stopper is the better design, and how do you know?

choices.label: Foam — it stopped the car 3 of 3 tries.
choices.why: Yes. The evidence is 3 of 3 for foam against 1 of 3 for cardboard.

choices.label: Cardboard — it is stiffer.
choices.why: Stiff is not the goal. The goal is stopping the car, and cardboard only stopped it 1 of 3.

choices.label: They are the same — both are stoppers.
choices.why: The data is not the same: 3 of 3 against 1 of 3.

rounds.finding: Foam stopped the car 3 of 3 tries. Cardboard stopped it 1 of 3. Evidence picks foam.

choices.label: one thing at a time.
choices.why: Right. Everything else stayed the same, so we know what caused each change.

choices.label: everything at once, to finish faster.
choices.why: Then we could not tell what caused each change. A fair test changes one thing.

choices.label: strong went 6 tiles, soft 2. Foam stopped 3 of 3.
choices.why: That matches every row of our data.

choices.label: the car stopped because it ran out of push.
choices.why: Something else slowed it: rubbing on the floor, or the stopper. Cars do not run out of push.

choices.label: one try is enough to be sure.
choices.why: We used 3 tries for each stopper to be more sure.

choices.label: pushes and pulls change motion. Evidence picks the better stopper.
choices.why: Yes. That is the whole investigation in one line.

choices.label: only hands can push or pull.
choices.why: Wind pushes sailboats and snowplows push snow. Pushes and pulls come from many things.
